summary: Backend Phase 2 testing for THE ROOM BARBERIA: 29/29 pytest tests passed (100%) covering approvals workflow (list/approve/reject/edge cases), employee management CRUD (list/create/update/delete with auth/duplicate/self-deletion guards), and dashboard data prerequisites (users count, month filter, user_id filter, location values). Fixed a real backend bug: jwt.JWTError → jwt.PyJWTError in /app/backend/server.py:64 which was causing 500 errors on invalid/malformed tokens instead of 401. All approval flows verified: pending entries auto-populate for vacation/permit; work/sick/other auto-approve; after approve/reject the entry is removed from /api/approvals list and status changes correctly.

minor.issue: update_user always re-hashes password (mandatory in payload). Frontend must always send a password on edit or it will set hash of empty/None and effectively lock the account. Consider making password optional on update.
No 'cannot modify own role' guard — an admin could demote themselves to employee and lose admin access.
Cleanup of time_entries uses string user_id which matches schema, OK. But there is no cascade for any other related data if added later.
Employees silently get only their own entries even when user_id query param is supplied for another user — no 403. Behaviour is safe but could be confusing; consider 403 if user_id != self.
Uses ObjectId(entry_id) without try/except — passing a malformed id will return 500 instead of 404. Same applies to /api/approvals/{id} and /api/users/{id}.
No validation on entry_type values (any string accepted) or on location values (any string accepted). Pydantic Literal/Enum recommended.

action_items: Optional: make password optional in PUT /api/users/{id} so admins can edit user info without resetting password every time.
Optional: add try/except around ObjectId() conversions to return 404 instead of 500 on malformed ids.
Optional: validate entry_type/location with Pydantic Literal/Enum to enforce ['work','vacation','sick','permit','other'] and ['Costabissara','Vicenza Est'].
Optional: prevent admin from changing own role to 'employee' to avoid lockout.
critical_code_review_comments: Fixed: jwt.JWTError attribute does not exist in PyJWT; replaced with jwt.PyJWTError (server.py line 64). Without the fix, every invalid token caused a 500 instead of 401.
PUT /api/users requires password on every update — likely unintended UX; admins editing names will inadvertently overwrite passwords (frontend must always send the same password back).
All ObjectId() conversions are unguarded — malformed ids will surface as 500 errors.
seed_data_creation: No persistent seed data. All test users/entries are created with TEST_ prefix and cleaned up at the end of each test class.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Backend API at EXPO_PUBLIC_BACKEND_URL (not EXPO_BACKEND_URL — note the PUBLIC infix used by this Expo project). Seed via POST /api/seed (idempotent). Admin: marius/marius2025. Approvals: only vacation+permit start pending; work/sick/other auto-approve. After PUT /api/approvals/{id} the entry leaves /api/approvals. Bug fixed this iteration: server.py used jwt.JWTError (does not exist in PyJWT) — now uses jwt.PyJWTError.
rca_of_issue: Latent 500 on invalid auth token: get_current_user caught jwt.JWTError which doesn't exist in PyJWT (that name belongs to python-jose). Result: AttributeError propagated as 500. Reproduced via: curl -H 'Authorization: Bearer invalid.token.here' /api/auth/me → 500. Fixed by replacing with jwt.PyJWTError (base class for all PyJWT errors); verified now returns 401.
